name: Tough74 V2
verdict: Bend test (TM_lenkimas, five strips 0.4 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0 / 1.5 mm against a 30/60/90° scale). The aim is not to grade the resin's strength but to show the printer delivers the properties the resin has. V: the thick strips (1.0 and 1.5 mm) broke near 30° but only under real force; the thinner ones bent further, 0.75 mm reached 90°. There is a pattern by thickness we do not chase. The resin stiffened as it stood. Verdict: tough, not brittle - which is what matters.
future: Resione pointed out that this printer has no pre-exposure wait - a pause before the UV comes on that lets a viscous resin flow back under the part. The firmware does not have it yet, and it is going into a future release. All the test prints so far came out true without it.
about: Resione's tough, wear-resistant resin: stiff and hard rather than brittle, and smooth straight off the plate.
take: Sharp down to the pixel limit, and a printed clip took 25 cycles without cracking. A 21 mm lattice cube printed standing on its corner came out square, every face at 21 mm.
stageNote: The lattice cube used at first came from another test set and turned out to be deformed, so a true cube was built from scratch. The first prints still leaned. A series of matched cubes printed since then came out square, and a 21 mm cube standing on its corner measured 21 mm on every face.

tests.txt: Repeated with a clean photo and a caliper: the cured strip is 0.10 mm thick at 8.5 s, 0.13 mm at 10 s and only 0.15 mm at 16 s. Flat and crisp from 10 s, which stays the setting.
Six of seven pillars straight and the detail clean, but it gripped the plate too hard to lift.

props.v: too strong - cannot be lifted without freezing

tests.txt: The same coupon at 10.0 s, reprinted for clean photos. Every bristle on the side printed - they only bent in the wash, being that thin - while the ones on top were too fine to print. Slots and checkerboard open.
Hardest first layer we have - 61 % of the plate in one layer. It held, and came off normally.

Not a strength rating - a check that the printer delivers the toughness the resin promises. Bent against the printed scale, the thick strips gave way near 30° only under real force and the thin ones bent further. Tough, not brittle.
Reprinted at 10.0 s: all seven pins stand, down to 0.30 mm - 2.3 pixels wide.

On a resin printer a bridge starts as one layer cured between two posts with nothing beneath it, then peeled off the film. All four spans held, up to 8 mm - how far apart supports can stand under a flat area.
A 21 mm lattice cube printed standing on its corner: every face measures 21 mm, edges straight.
